sourceBindings.text: A wilted or discoloured leaf is an observation. Build a testable explanation, check soil, roots and weather, then justify water and nutrient actions with the right source, rate, time and place.
Separate observed symptoms from a diagnosis in all four cases; investigate drainage, cold soil, root function, weather and test results before treating a supposed water or nutrient shortage.

Build a conditional water-and-fertilizer response using all four 4R decisions, stating which evidence sets fertilizer rate and why calcium nitrate is an N-and-Ca source rather than a complete NPK product.

Work through two distinct cases in full, explain and defend one during discussion, and compare the other source cases without prescribing a fixed watering or fertilizing calendar from appearance alone.

sourceBindings.text: Sort observed wilt, colour, leaf age, standing water and temperature from the possible causes; propose a field check that could disprove each diagnosis.
Match N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S, Fe, Mn and Zn to the correct element name and nutrient group, then use old-leaf yellowing, purple maize and old-leaf margins as qualified clues.
For a chosen case, supply right source, rate evidence, timing condition and placement with water priority and potential loss pathway.
Take two different case cards, complete observation/hypothesis/test/water/4R sheets for both, and present and defend one while comparing the other cases.
If a student jumps from one symptom to one fertilizer or watering order, route back to observation and alternative hypotheses.

These online tasks rehearse reasoning only. Typed completeness and correct choices do not establish a diagnosis, a real field treatment or criterion mastery; the case explanations need trainer review.

sourceBindings.text: symptom
An observed plant change that can prompt investigation but does not alone prove its cause.
hypothesis
A plausible explanation that can be tested against further observations or measurements.
temporary wilting
A reversible drop in turgor that may appear when daytime loss exceeds uptake, even before soil moisture is known.
waterlogging
Saturation that restricts oxygen to roots and may limit their uptake of water and nutrients.
macronutrient
An essential nutrient needed in relatively larger amount, including N, P, K, Ca, Mg and S.
micronutrient
An essential nutrient needed in smaller amount, such as Fe, Mn or Zn.
4R nutrient stewardship
Choosing the right nutrient source, rate, time and place for the crop and site.
band placement
A fertilizer strip placed at a specified position near roots or seed row, subject to product and crop safety limits.
calcium nitrate
A fertilizer source of nitrogen and calcium; it does not by itself supply a complete N-P-K balance.
